comparator.name: Bestuurs- en organisatiewetenschap (Public Administration and Organisation Science)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum defines a three-year, 180-EC bachelor with a 142.5-EC major and 37.5 EC of free profiling space. Year one contains eight compulsory 7.5-EC courses. Year two contains five compulsory 7.5-EC courses, one 7.5-EC choice and a 15-EC qualitative-research course. Year three preserves four 7.5-EC free-choice courses, the 7.5-EC public-issues analysis and advice capstone, and a 22.5-EC graduation trajectory culminating in the bachelor thesis. The public prospective page confirms that the programme integrates public administration, organisation science, law, economics, political science and anthropology around public problems. No formal route or specialisation requires selection, and the components account for exactly 180 EC.

alternatives.label: Public governance, policy and organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates comparative government, public law, policy, public economics, organisation theory, leadership, communication and mixed research methods around public problems.
alternatives.concept: A broad public-administration and organisation programme examining how governments, institutions and public organisations make and implement decisions. Political science, law, sociology, economics, leadership and communication are combined with quantitative, qualitative and independent research.
progression: Law, comparative politics and sociology foundations precede constitutional and international law, EU politics and advanced social theory. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics and organisational leadership; Law, Society & Justice precedes both upper-level law courses. Every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Public organisations, leadership and management
alternatives.labelReason: Leadership, organisational behaviour, diversity management, strategy, governance, negotiation and communication organise a genuinely different route centred on people and change in public-purpose organisations.
alternatives.concept: Focuses on how public-purpose organisations lead people, manage diversity, communicate, negotiate and respond to digital and institutional change. Business and organisation foundations are integrated with politics, public economics, law, sociology and mixed research methods.
progression: Business, leadership, law, politics and sociology foundations precede strategy, diversity management, organisational psychology, international governance, business law and negotiation. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all courses that formally require it; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes strategy, international governance and business law. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad governance route, this programme replaces human rights, economics foundations, international law, sustainability governance, EU politics and historical research with business foundations, personal leadership, organisational communication, diversity management, digital transformation, international business governance and transnational business law. Seven courses differ in each direction, and the changes follow its organisation-and-leadership focus.

blocks: Public governance, institutions, law and policy
Both examine institutional decision-making and public policy; UCR focuses on the European Union rather than Dutch public administration.
Both analyse societal problems and institutional contexts; UCR supplies a general sociological foundation.
Both use political thought to examine authority, leadership and public responsibility.
Both address constitutional constraints on public authority; UCR is comparative constitutional law rather than Dutch administrative law.
Both compare political institutions and their effects on public decision-making.
Both analyse policy, interests, power and implementation; UCR applies these questions to sustainability governance.
The official restricted-choice component is preserved without inventing an elective.
UCR has normative philosophy, but no sufficiently direct philosophy-of-science counterpart is scheduled.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space is preserved without invented content.
Both examine organisational perspectives, behaviour and interaction among organisational actors.
Both address management and organisational operation; UCR provides general business foundations rather than public-service management.
Both examine how organisations respond to change; UCR focuses on strategic digital transformation.
Both develop strategic analysis and advisory skills for complex organisational problems; UCR emphasises negotiation and strategy.
The integrated practice course has no single UCR course counterpart; relevant practical skills are distributed across leadership and communication courses.
Both introduce research design, quantitative methods and statistics.

Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing, interpretation and reflexivity.
The 22.5-EC B&O graduation trajectory culminates in independent public-administration and organisation research; UCR's optional independent research is shown as a comparison-only element.

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers the broad public-governance, policy, institutions, law, economics and research core. The two remaining direct generator interests—improving public administration and management, and understanding power, leadership and public responsibility—support a coherent organisation-and-leadership route with seven distinct courses in each direction. All other rows are curricular topics, examples or outcomes that reinforce these two concepts rather than independently generating a third direction; a third programme would require inventing a new substantive interest. Production therefore stops at two.

notes.text: Utrecht University organises Public Administration and Organisation Science as a dedicated sequence in public administration, organisation science, public-service management and annual organisation-based research. UCR can combine political science, law, sociology, economics, leadership, communication and research methods into two coherent programmes, but it does not reproduce the same dedicated public-administration and public-organisation sequence; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
